item.title: Beyond The Sole: How Nigerian Artist Eugene Is Turning Waste Into Beauty For A Better World
item.description: An art project that started as a final-year assessment at Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State, Nigeria, has turned into a full-time career for Konboye Eugene. In his studio in Kuto, Abeokuta, Ogun State, the Nigerian artist is giving discarded footwear a new lease of life, transforming them into colourful portraits. “I’ve been a full-time studio practitioner for about seven years now. I started when I was in my final year at Auchi Polytechnic, where I studied painting,” Eugene said. “It started as an assignment for me when I was in school. But over the course of my practice, I have become a bit more environmentally aware.” ﻿ Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Materials ‘Everywhere, Anywhere’ Eugene’s craft draws attention to the environmental impact of discarded footwear and the need for better ways to manage waste. “I source my material through landfills, the streets, literally everywhere, anywhere,” he added. This image shows Eugene assessing discarded footwear he used for his artwork. (Photo: ChannelsTV/Kenny Akinwunmi) The artist shares the detailed process of how he brings each work of art to life. “My process entails getting the materials first, after which we wash them. After we wash them, we have to select and separate them according to their colours, tones, and values.” “I work in two different ways. There’s the assemblage part, where I assemble the footwear. And there’s also the tapestry, where I have to break them into tiny circles and fix them together using copper and aluminium wire,” Eugene explained. Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Creating each piece of artwork comes with its challenges, as Eugene says the process can take between two and six months, depending on its size and complexity. “There are a whole lot of challenges that come with the work. There are times when we’re working and have creative blockages. And also, because we work with sharp objects like knives, needles, and all that, there’s also the hazard that comes with it. “I think we work between two to six months, depending on the size and complexity of what we’re working on in the studio,” he said. For Eugene, the message goes beyond the finished artwork, as he hopes his work will change how people perceive and handle discarded materials. “These are materials that are known to be non-biodegradable, meaning all the footwear that I’ve used over the course of the years, they’re all out there. So we are creating awareness through this work so people know what and how to manage their footwear and other fashion waste,” he noted. ‘Reduce, Reuse, Recycle’ Climate change expert Olumide Idowu agrees with Eugene and is calling for more

item.title: Bomb threats force evacuation of schools across Italy
item.description: Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday following a series of bomb threats, which Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described as hoaxes, insisting that there was no concrete danger. The threats, which reportedly affected about 6,000 schools, according to Italian news agency Ansa, citing the Education Ministry, also prompted security concerns in Britain and Ireland, where threatening emails were sent to hundreds of schools. Meloni convened a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs on Wednesday to review the incidents. Although it was unclear how many Italian schools evacuated their students, crowds of schoolchildren were seen outside educational institutions in different parts of the country. Some students said they had to leave their classrooms hurriedly, abandoning their belongings while awaiting police checks. A 19-year-old student at Rome’s Virgilio High School, Sofia De Ponte, told AFP that the school’s principal announced that a bomb threat had been received by email before ordering an evacuation. “The principal came out into the courtyard and told us that an email had come in, a bomb threat, and right after that the building was evacuated,” she said. De Ponte said the police had yet to arrive because “there’s a long waiting list with all the schools”. “We’re still here waiting,” another student, Elena Sicignano, 19, said. At Brera school in Milan, art teacher Violetta Uboldi said some students appeared delighted by the unexpected break from classes. “I think there was a cry of joy because school was over. That was the reaction,” she said. However, a 16-year-old student, Angelica, said the situation initially caused panic because a teacher had told them it was not a drill. Italian media reported that the threatening email was purportedly signed by a person identified as “Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan”. The message claimed that an explosive device had been placed inside a school building and could be detonated remotely. Government Rules Out Immediate Danger The Italian government sought to reassure the public, saying preliminary security checks had not uncovered evidence of an imminent threat. In a Facebook post, Meloni said: “At present, based on the checks carried out, no element has emerged that would suggest there is a concrete danger.” She added that the reports appeared to be part of a strategy designed to cause alarm and concern, adding that investigations were ongoing. Antonello Giannelli, president of the ANP association of Italian school heads, also described the threats as clearly fake. However, he warned that the incident demonstrated how irresponsible actions, amplified by modern communication tools, could cause widespread disruption. “We hope that full light will quickly be shed on the origin of these threats and that those responsible will be identified,” he said. item.title: EU commits €112m to Nigeria’s security, migration management
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The European Union (EU) has committed €112 million to support Nigeria’s security operations and migration management efforts as part of measures to strengthen bilateral cooperation between both sides. The EU disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday following the visit of its Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, Mr Magnus Brunner, to Abuja, where he held meetings with key members of the Nigerian government. The funding comprises €66 million for migration-related projects, €26 million for security interventions, including efforts to tackle the proliferation of small arms and drug trafficking, and €20 million under the European Peace Facility to support Nigeria’s counterterrorism efforts. During the visit, Brunner met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu; Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi (SAN); Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo; and Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro. The visit came a day after Nigeria and the EU signed the EU-Nigeria Readmission Agreement, aimed at strengthening cooperation on migration management and facilitating the return of Nigerians who do not have the right to remain in EU member states. The EU said its migration partnership with Nigeria had recorded significant improvements in recent years, particularly through cooperation between Nigerian authorities and European agencies, including Europol, Eurojust and Frontex. It added that the partnership had expanded beyond migration to cover security, trade, regional economic cooperation and other areas of mutual interest. According to the statement, bilateral relations gained further momentum following the eighth EU-Nigeria Ministerial Meeting held in Abuja in March, with the participation of the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, Kaja Kallas. The EU also disclosed that its Global Gateway initiative was being implemented in Nigeria through several projects across different sectors by the EU and its member states under the Team Europe approach. Speaking on the partnership, Brunner said: “Nigeria is a key partner for Europe, and our ties are steadily growing stronger. Together we are turning dialogue into action: more security, better migration management, joining forces to bring results. We are turning the huge potential of our partnership into mutual benefit.” He said the visit provided an opportunity to review the partnership, advance cooperation on shared priorities and prepare for further engagement between both sides in areas beyond migration and security. item.title: ADC accuses APC govt of sealing Arewa House to stop Atiku’s consultation
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of frustrating opposition activities after the Kaduna State Government allegedly sealed the historic Arewa House ahead of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar’s planned consultation with Northern stakeholders. The party said the development was part of a growing pattern of attempts to obstruct its political engagements, warning that denying its candidate access to a proposed venue for consultation amounted to using public authority against democratic competition. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, on Tuesday, the party also expressed concern over the release of the authenticated copy of Justice Peter Lifu’s judgment on the final day of the constitutionally prescribed seven-day period for furnishing parties with court decisions. The ADC said the timing had left it with little time to study the judgment and prepare its next legal steps, but vowed to pursue all available lawful remedies. Citing Section 294(1) of the 1999 Constitution, the party noted that courts are required to furnish parties with duly authenticated copies of their decisions within seven days of delivery. On the Arewa House controversy, Atiku said: “My campaign team had proposed the Arewa House as the venue for our consultation with stakeholders on Thursday and, today, the APC government decided to seal the building.” The ADC described Arewa House as part of the shared heritage of Northern Nigeria’s diverse peoples, arguing that its closure ahead of the proposed consultation was an affront to their culture and dignity. Drawing a parallel with its campaign flag-off in Sokoto, the party alleged that the APC-led government had similarly attempted to frustrate the event, but that the people had stood firm. “This is a troubling pattern,” the party said. Holding President Bola Tinubu and the APC politically responsible, the ADC said the ruling party should not deploy public authority to restrict opposition activities or undermine Nigerians’ freedom to make political choices. “An outgoing president and a ruling party should respect democratic competition, not use public authority to impede the opposition, restrict political consultation or weaken Nigerians’ right to choose,” the party said. The ADC vowed to press ahead with its political engagements despite the alleged obstruction, thanking Nigerians for their support and solidarity. It said it would continue its consultations, pursue its legal rights and take its message of a new direction to the electorate. item.title: 2027: I’ll protect Christians, Muslims, other faiths — Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has pledged to protect Christians, Muslims and adherents of other faiths in Nigeria, saying religious freedom must become a central pillar of the country’s security and conflict prevention strategy. Hashim made the pledge in a policy brief submitted to the United States Congress and the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), ahead of a US House hearing on Nigeria. He acknowledged the persecution of Christians in parts of the country, including attacks on churches, killings of pastors and destruction of communities, but cautioned against portraying Nigeria’s religious crisis exclusively as a conflict between Christians and Muslims. He said members of other religious and ethnic communities, including Shia Muslims, minority sects and Hausa Muslim communities, also faced persecution and discrimination. “Christians in northern and central Nigeria face persecution. Churches have been burned, villages destroyed, and pastors killed. This is real. “But Shia Muslims, minority sects, and Hausa Muslim communities also face persecution and discrimination. Framing Nigeria as Christians versus Muslims divides Nigeria. Framing it as all victims versus violent extremism unites Nigeria,” he said. The Accord candidate argued that religious freedom should be treated not merely as a human rights issue but also as an essential instrument for preventing conflicts and strengthening national security. “When people cannot worship freely, they feel excluded. When killers are not punished, impunity grows. When impunity grows, communities form militias. When militias grow, extremists recruit from them,” he said. Hashim added that protecting churches, mosques and cultural centres across the country was necessary to prevent extremism from taking root. He pledged that, if elected in 2027, his administration would develop and implement a National Policy Framework on Religious Freedom for Conflict Prevention and Countering Violent Extremism. As part of the proposed measures, he said his administration would convene a National Summit within its first 90 days, bringing together victims, the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), Shia leaders, Hausa cultural representatives, women, young people and internally displaced persons. He also proposed a National Religious Freedom for Conflict Prevention and Countering Violent Extremism Act within 180 days of assuming office. According to him, the proposed legislation would criminalise religious persecution, hate incitement and forced displacement. Hashim further proposed the establishment of an independent national commission, with offices in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, to report to the National Assembly. item.title: Nigeria crude oil production hits 1.68mbpd – NUPRC
item.description: Nigeria produced an average of 1.687 million barrels of crude oil and condensate per day in October 2026, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has said. Data released by the commission on Wednesday showed that daily production peaked at 1.79 million barrels per day (bpd), while the lowest output during the month was 1.60 million bpd. The data showed that crude oil production, excluding condensate, averaged 1.51 million barrels per day (mbpd) during the review period. This represented 101 per cent of Nigeria’s 1.5 million bpd production quota allocated by the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC). According to the report, Nigeria had met its assigned OPEC crude oil production quota for six consecutive months. It said the country produced 1.53 million bpd in May, 1.55 million bpd in June, 1.51 million bpd in July, 1.50 million bpd in August, 1.53 million bpd in September and 1.51 million bpd in October. The report, however, indicated a 1.7 per cent month-on-month decline in crude oil production. It attributed the relatively stable performance in recent months to improved operational stability, production uptime and crude evacuation efficiency. The commission said the sustained performance in October reflected the commitment of operators and industry stakeholders to improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity and enhancing production reliability across the upstream sector. A breakdown of daily average crude oil and condensate production by terminals and streams showed that Forcados Terminal recorded the highest output of 318.49 thousand barrels per day (kbpd). Bonny Terminal followed with 311.02 kbpd, while Qua Iboe Terminal recorded 173.97 kbpd. Escravos Oil Terminal produced an average of 134.67 kbpd, while Bonga ranked fifth with 106.65 kbpd of crude oil and condensate.(NAN) The post Nigeria crude oil production hits 1.68mbpd – NUPRC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Russian ambassador to the US dies ‘suddenly’ – Foreign Ministry
item.description: Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died “suddenly” at the age of 66 after just one and a half years in the job, Moscow’s foreign ministry announced Wednesday. The ministry called Darchiev an “outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader and a kind colleague”. He was appointed in March 2025. Moscow did not give more details on the death. Darchiev previously served as Russia’s ambassador to Canada between 2014 and 2021. He was appointed to the US role last year, shortly after President Donald Trump returned to power, and several years into Moscow’s Ukraine offensive that has pitted Russia against the West. Darchiev was a specialist in Russia-US relations and was the director of the foreign ministry’s North America department between 2021-2024. In 2022, when Russia attacked Ukraine, Darchiev called the move a “necessary measure”. The post Russian ambassador to the US dies ‘suddenly’ – Foreign Ministry appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kane says England appearance record a ‘testament to dedication’
item.description: England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions’ appearance record in Thursday’s Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a “testament to all the dedication” that has gone into his career. When Kane leads England out at Wembley to earn his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton since 1990. It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or. The 33-year-old Kane is also England’s record scorer with 91 goals, as well as holding Tottenham Hotspur’s all-time mark with 280. Since leaving Spurs to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level. He has amassed 156 goals for the German club, finally winning the first silverware of his career with Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026. But breaking Shilton’s long-standing record also matters to Kane, who told a pre-match press conference on Wednesday: “It’s definitely up there as the biggest (achievement). “I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don’t see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career.” For all Kane’s brilliance, England have not won a major men’s international trophy since lifting the 1966 World Cup on home soil. And Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as England were beaten by Argentina in the semi-finals of the World Cup. – ‘Beautiful occasion’ – England were leading 1-0 until late in the game but could not score again, with manager Thomas Tuchel criticised for packing the team’s defence only for Argentina to score twice late on as Kane was denied a first appearance in a World Cup final. “In terms of what’s next, I don’t like to put limits — 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible,” added Kane. “We’ve done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages. I’m feeling really good, and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve.” Tuchel, speaking earlier Wednesday, was coy when asked if Kane was England’s greatest footballer. “I don’t know. He’s up there of course. It’s now proven. It’s always nice if things are proven in sports — he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games. “Tomorrow he will start for us and as captain. It’s a big occasion to present the Ballon d’Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded in the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches; it’s a beautiful occasion.” England are all but guaranteed a place in March’s Nations League quarter-finals, regardless of Thursday’s result, having thrashed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka last month in what Tuchel labelled a “freak result”. “We expect a reaction from Croatia and we expect to overcome this mental challenge for us,” Tuchel said Wednesday. item.title: 2027: Obi pledges security, jobs, food for Nigerians
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has pledged to tackle insecurity, unemployment and hunger, saying his administration would build a Nigeria where no citizen is left behind if elected in 2027. Obi made the pledge during a town hall meeting in Benue State as part of his 2027 campaign activities and a humanitarian visit to Yelewata community in Guma Local Government Area of the state. Accompanied by his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, the former Anambra State governor said he was seeking the support of Benue residents to secure and unite the country. He said a new Nigeria was possible, promising decisive action against kidnapping and other security threats. “If we are in government, nobody will witness what is happening in the country today. “If you kidnap school children or kill anybody and try to run into the bush, we will go into the bush with you and we will get you. We must stop this act. Nigeria must be secured,” he said. Obi also promised that no Nigerian would be allowed to go to bed hungry, while criticising the management of the country’s resources under President Bola Tinubu. According to him, although Nigeria has more money under the current administration, citizens are yet to feel the impact. “Nigeria has gotten more money but citizens do not know where the money is going,” he said. The NDC candidate also claimed that there was no ongoing Federal Government project in Benue State, promising to prioritise development, job creation and youth empowerment if elected. “We want to build a better society for you. For the youths, we want to ensure you finish school and be able to start your own business or get a job. “Those with no jobs today, we assure you of our commitment that you will have something to do. Youth unemployment is unacceptable. We will empower the people through agriculture. “We will build a society where a child of nobody will be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. He added that his administration would tackle corruption to ensure public funds were deployed for the common good, while investing in healthcare and education. Obi visits Yelewata attack victims Earlier, Obi visited Yelewata community in Guma LGA to sympathise with residents and families of those affected by the June 2025 attack. The presidential candidate also paid a courtesy visit to the Tor Tiv, His Royal Majesty, Prof. James Ayatse, at his palace in Gboko Local Government Area. Ayatse thanked Obi for the visit, prayed for his protection and a successful engagement in the state, and called for continued prayers for Benue and Nigeria. Obi told the traditional ruler that he was in the state for both humanitarian and political engagements, adding that he considered it important to visit the palace to seek his royal blessing and hold discussions. item.title: FG targets 1,000 CNG stations nationwide, commissions five in Lagos
item.description: Stations target 8,400 vehicles daily – MDGIF By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor The Federal Government has unveiled plans to expand Nigeria’s Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) refuelling network to 1,000 stations nationwide, including 500 additional facilities, as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs and deepen domestic gas utilisation. The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Mr Ekperikpe Ekpo, disclosed this during the commissioning of five CNG daughter and last-mile retail stations developed by IBILE Oil and Gas Corporation, with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), in Lagos. The facilities, located at Idimu, Ogolonto, Abule-Egba, Ajah and Oko-Oba, are expected to bring natural gas closer to motorists, commercial transport operators and businesses. Ekpo said: “The President has specifically directed the expansion of CNG infrastructure nationwide, including an additional 500 CNG refuelling stations towards a planned national network of 1,000 stations, with emphasis on ensuring that the benefits translate into lower transportation costs for Nigerians.” According to him, each facility has a CNG compression capacity of 24,000 standard cubic metres per day and storage capacity of 9,800 standard cubic metres. He said the success of the initiative would be measured by its impact on transportation costs, businesses and households. “Our objective is therefore not simply to count the number of stations commissioned. Success must ultimately be measured by impact: whether the infrastructure helps reduce operating costs for transporters and businesses, whether those savings reach commuters, and whether Nigerian families begin to feel tangible relief,” he stated. Similarly, the Executive Director of MDGIF, Mr Oluwole Adama, said the five stations had a combined gas storage capacity of 45,640 standard cubic metres and could serve about 8,400 vehicles daily at full capacity. He said: “Together, the five stations at Abule Egba, Ajah, Oko-Oba, Idimu and Ogolonto can hold 45,640 standard cubic metres of gas. At full capacity, they can fill about 8,400 cars per day, using natural gas produced right here in Nigeria.” Adama said the facilities would help reduce fuel costs for commercial drivers and fleet operators, while creating employment opportunities in operations, safety, maintenance, logistics and technical services. “For the commercial driver, this means less time in a queue and more time on the road earning. For the fleet owner, it means a fuel bill that is easier to plan for. For the rest of us, it means cleaner air on the roads we share,” he stated. He, however, stressed the importance of reliable gas supply, regular maintenance and safety, saying: “The real achievement will be safe operations, reliable supply, professional maintenance and lasting public confidence.” Meanwhile, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of IBILE Oil and Gas Corporation, Mr Temitayo Gbajumo, said the corporation was targ

item.title: Google commits $600,000 to child online safety in Nigeria
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Google has committed $600,000 to support initiatives aimed at improving online safety for children in Nigeria, including a nationwide study of adolescents’ internet use and digital safety training for parents, teachers and young people. The technology company said the initiatives would be implemented through the TechSocietal Development Foundation and Tech Hive Advisory. The programmes include a $600,000 support package for TechSocietal and the introduction of Google’s Meet LEO (Learn and Explore Online) child online safety programme in Nigeria. The announcements follow public consultations by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), which found that 93.5 per cent of Nigerians were concerned about online harms affecting children. Under the TechSocietal programme, the foundation will conduct a survey of 2,000 adolescents across the country’s six geopolitical zones and train 5,000 teachers and school administrators. It will also train 200 community champions, who are expected to reach up to 10,000 parents and caregivers. Google’s support comprises $550,000 in funding and $50,000 in Google Ad Grants. Meet LEO, being piloted in sub-Saharan Africa for the first time, will be delivered by Tech Hive Advisory across four states. The programme is expected to train 500 educators and youth leaders, who will in turn share online safety guidance with 2,500 students and community members. The training will cover digital safety tools, including Google Family Link, SafeSearch and YouTube Supervised Experiences. Country Director of Google Nigeria, Olumide Balogun, said protecting children online should not deprive them of the opportunities offered by the internet. “It takes a village to raise a child, and today that village extends into the digital world, where protecting our children must never mean disconnecting them from their future,” he said. Balogun added that the initiatives would combine local research with educator training to help Nigerian children navigate the internet safely. National Commissioner of the NDPC, Dr Vincent Olatunji, said protecting children online required cooperation among government agencies, technology platforms, educators and families. “The NDPC’s recent national consultations made it clear that Nigerians are deeply concerned about the risks young people face online. “By combining local evidence with hands-on digital skills, we are building a safer, more empowering digital environment where every Nigerian child can learn, explore and thrive,” he said. Lead Partner at Tech Hive Advisory, Ridwan Oloyede, said the Meet LEO pilot would provide practical online safety tools to educators and youth leaders, enabling them to extend the training to more young people. item.title: 2027: SDP names Tanko coordinator of 12,000-member campaign council
item.description: …Adebayo alleges growing intolerance under APC …Party promises to tackle poverty, insecurity By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, appointing Dr Yunusa Tanko, former Northern Coordinator of the Obidient Movement, as its National Coordinator. The inauguration, held in Abuja on Wednesday, brought together party leaders, candidates and other stakeholders to strategise for the 2027 general elections. Inaugurating the council, the SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as its chairman, charged members to run an issue-based and people-centred campaign anchored on the Constitution, Electoral Act, Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. Gombe said Nigeria was at a defining moment and urged party members to work towards defeating President Bola Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. He called on members of the campaign council to demonstrate commitment, discipline and effective organisation to secure electoral victories for the party. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC Guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. The SDP chairman identified insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, poverty, institutional weaknesses and declining public confidence in governance as some of the major challenges confronting the country. He said Nigerians deserved purposeful leadership, economic opportunities, social justice, security and accountability, adding that the SDP was determined to provide an alternative founded on equity, freedom, inclusive development and good governance. Gombe urged members of the council to take the party’s message to communities across the country, engage voters respectfully and demonstrate through their conduct that the party deserved public trust. He said the party’s mission was to build a strong, united and nationwide political organisation capable of delivering electoral victories at all levels in 2027 while contributing to the preservation and strengthening of Nigeria’s democracy. In his remarks, the SDP presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, warned against what he described as growing political intolerance and dictatorial tendencies under the All Progressives Congress (APC), cautioning that attempts to restrict opposition activities could undermine democracy. item.title: Nigeria ready to host 126 countries at 2026 PR forum
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has declared its readiness to host the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF), with representatives from more than 126 countries and leading international institutions expected at the global event scheduled to hold in Abuja from November 15 to 22. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, gave the assurance at a world press conference in Abuja on Wednesday. The forum, to be hosted under the leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as Chief Host, is expected to bring together global public relations experts, communication professionals, policymakers and representatives of major international organisations to discuss the future of responsible communication. Speaking at the event, Idris described Nigeria’s selection as host as significant recognition of the country’s growing influence in global communication and public relations. He appreciated the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the African Public Relations Association (APRA) for entrusting Nigeria with the responsibility of hosting the international and continental gatherings simultaneously. The minister noted that Nigeria would become the first country in West Africa and the second in Africa to host the World Public Relations Forum, describing the opportunity as a major milestone for the country and the continent. According to him, the forum would provide Nigeria with an important platform to showcase its institutional capacity, strengthen international partnerships and contribute to conversations shaping the global communication industry. With the theme, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World,” the 2026 forum is expected to address critical challenges confronting the communication industry, particularly the growing influence of digital platforms, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Idris warned that the rapid transformation of the information environment had heightened concerns over misinformation, disinformation and the erosion of public trust. He stressed that communication professionals must remain committed to truth, accuracy, transparency and ethical conduct. The minister maintained that the responsibility of public relations practitioners should extend beyond protecting institutional reputations and promoting organisational interests to safeguarding the public interest and ensuring that citizens have access to credible information. He also highlighted the Federal Government’s support for the establishment of the UNESCO Category 2 International Media and Information Literacy Institute (IMILI) in Abuja. He described the initiative as a strategic investment in building an informed society, particularly among young people, by equipping citizens with the knowledge and skills to identify misleading information and navigate the increasingly complex digital environment. item.title: How Do Enterprise Brands Scale TikTok Influencer Marketing?
item.description: Running a TikTok campaign with five creators is manageable. Running campaigns with dozens or hundreds of creators across different products, countries, internal teams, and agencies is a very different challenge. For large brands, the real question is not simply how to find more influencers. It is how to scale TikTok influencer marketing without losing control over creative quality, brand standards, budgets, reporting, and local relevance. That requires systems. Brands need repeatable ways to identify creators, review content, approve campaigns, manage payments, protect the brand, measure results, and learn from previous activity. A specialist TikTok marketing agency can support that process by bringing creator strategy, campaign operations, paid media, and performance measurement into one coordinated structure. The goal is to move from individual creator activations to a repeatable marketing channel. To Scale TikTok Influencer Marketing, Start With the Operating Model Before adding more creators, enterprise brands need to decide how the influencer program will actually operate. Large organizations may have global marketing teams, regional managers, product divisions, legal departments, procurement teams, local agencies, and paid media specialists involved in the same campaign. Without clear ownership, adding more creators can simply add more complexity. Most large influencer programs generally follow one of three models: Centralized: A global team controls strategy, creator selection, budgets, approvals, and reporting. Decentralized: Regional teams manage their own campaigns independently. Hybrid: Central teams establish standards while regional teams control local execution. For multinational brands, the hybrid model can often provide a useful balance. The organization can standardize contracts, reporting, creator-vetting requirements, brand safety, and campaign objectives while allowing regional teams to adapt language, creators, cultural references, and content formats. Vanguard has highlighted the growing importance of having a clear digital strategy rather than simply maintaining a social media presence. Its coverage of why businesses need digital strategy reflects the same principle. Scale should begin with structure, not volume. Standardize What Does Not Need to Change One of the easiest ways for influencer programs to become inefficient is for every campaign to start from zero. Enterprise teams should standardize repeatable processes such as: Creator vetting criteria Campaign brief templates Contract structures Content approval stages Usage rights Disclosure requirements Brand safety checks Reporting definitions Payment processes Performance dashboards This does not mean every campaign should look identical. item.title: CAC, EY warn directors against governance failures
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) has warned company directors against treating regulatory compliance as the sole responsibility of company secretaries, saying weak corporate records and governance failures could undermine business credibility, investment prospects and access to credit. The Registrar-General and Chief Executive Officer of CAC, Hussaini Ishaq Magaji, gave the warning at the 2026 Audit Committee Transformation Summit organised by Ernst & Young (EY) in Lagos on Wednesday. Magaji said directors’ responsibilities extended beyond strategy, profitability and risk management to protecting the integrity of their companies’ legal identities. He noted that outdated corporate records, undisclosed changes in ownership and failure to file annual returns could expose companies to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage and diminished investor confidence. According to him, “Directors must demonstrate diligence, transparency and accountability by ensuring accurate corporate records, timely statutory filings and proper disclosure of persons with significant control. “The era of filing annual returns as an annual ritual is over. The Corporate Affairs Commission is asking Nigerian boards and companies to move beyond merely filing annual returns towards continuous accountability, transparent ownership, accurate records and credible governance.” He added that companies with transparent ownership structures and disciplined governance would be better positioned to attract investments, secure credit, participate in public procurement and pursue business partnerships. Also speaking, Amina Maida, who represented the Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), said effective audit committees were essential to strengthening corporate resilience amid technological changes, cybersecurity threats and evolving regulatory requirements. She said the NCC issued corporate governance guidelines for the communications industry in 2025, outlining board and committee responsibilities, including risk management, internal controls and audit oversight. In his welcome address, EY Regional Managing Partner, West Africa, Anthony Oputa, said audit committees were performing their oversight responsibilities in an increasingly complex environment shaped by evolving regulatory expectations, geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, technological disruption, sustainability considerations and significant changes in financial reporting. Oputa, who was represented by Jamiu Olakisan, Assurance Leader, EY West Africa, said the developments were placing greater demands on audit committees to strengthen accounting and internal control systems, enhance corporate transparency, safeguard audit quality and reinforce stakeholder confidence. item.title: Kidnapping: Afenifere seeks sophisticated weapons for Amotekun
item.description: …Demands drones, forest surveillance, grassroots intelligence, full LG autonomy By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has called for a comprehensive overhaul of the South-West’s security architecture, urging governments to equip the Western Nigeria Security Network, codenamed Amotekun, with sophisticated weapons and modern surveillance technology to tackle kidnapping and other violent crimes. The organisation also called for the deployment of drones, improved forest surveillance, coordinated security operations and stronger grassroots intelligence gathering to curb the activities of kidnappers and armed gangs across the region. Afenifere warned that persistent attacks on highways, forests and rural communities exposed gaps in existing security arrangements, insisting that governments must move beyond security meetings and adopt more effective operational strategies. It further cautioned that poverty, educational deprivation and youth unemployment could sustain a recruitment pipeline for bandits and other criminal networks, urging authorities to combine security operations with sustained social and economic interventions. Afenifere’s National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, made the demands in a statement issued against the backdrop of recent abductions along the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan highway and at the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria, FRIN, Ibadan, on Wednesday. The latest incidents included the abduction of travellers heading to Ibadan from Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State, last Tuesday, with their abductors reportedly demanding a ransom of N25 million. One of the victims was identified as Mr Dapo, a recent National Youth Service Corps graduate who had just completed his national service in Edo State. The incident came weeks after prospective corps members travelling from Ibadan were abducted in Imo State on October 1, 2026. Similarly, the kidnapping of victims at FRIN, along the Ibadan–Ijebu-Ode highway, raised fresh concerns, as the location had reportedly witnessed a similar incident a few months earlier. Although the victims were eventually rescued or released, Afenifere said their freedom should not overshadow the recurring nature of the attacks and the threat they posed to residents, commuters and economic activities. Ajayi said, “We are deeply saddened that these disheartening incidents are occurring at all, as they remind us that much still needs to be done to secure the people and ensure their safety.” The organisation described the incidents as part of a disturbing pattern of violent crimes across the Yoruba-speaking states and adjoining areas. It cited the reported beheading of a farmer in Itesiwaju Local Government Area of Oyo State, the kidnapping of Prince Michael Folarin in Igbeti and the abduction of a 33-year-old poultry farmer, Mr Ooreoluwa Osonuga, in Ogun State. item.title: 2027: I’d have joined Rainbow Coalition if still in politics — Ladoja
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, has said he would have joined the Rainbow Coalition if he were still active in partisan politics, but noted that his position as a traditional ruler requires him to remain politically neutral. Ladoja said although he appreciated the political initiative behind the coalition, his traditional role demanded fairness, neutrality and equal treatment of all political tendencies, irrespective of party affiliations. The monarch spoke on Wednesday when he received a delegation of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) National Working Committee, led by the party’s National Secretary, Senator Samuel Anyanwu, at his palace in Ibadan. The delegation, which included members of the party’s national leadership and its governorship candidate in Oyo State, Hazeem Gbolarumi, paid homage to the monarch and formally presented the candidate to him ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking during the visit, Ladoja said his political disposition would have been different if he were still actively involved in partisan politics. “If I were still a politician, I would have joined the Rainbow Coalition. But now that I am a traditional ruler, my responsibility is different. “I have to accommodate everybody, irrespective of the political party they belong to. I cannot take sides with any political party or candidate. My duty is to receive everybody, advise them and admonish them where necessary,” the monarch said. He stressed that traditional rulers had important roles to play in sustaining democratic stability, particularly during electioneering periods, adding that their influence should be deployed towards promoting peaceful political engagement rather than deepening divisions. The Olubadan also said Nigeria needed a trusted leader capable of commanding public confidence, inspiring national unity and providing purposeful leadership amid the country’s numerous challenges. According to him, the country requires leadership anchored on credibility, integrity and the ability to earn the trust of the people. He urged politicians to place national interest above personal ambitions and partisan considerations, stressing that the political process should be guided by responsibility and genuine commitment to national development. Ladoja also appealed to political stakeholders to conduct themselves in ways that would preserve the peace and stability of the country as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum. Earlier, Anyanwu said the PDP delegation’s visit was part of efforts to sustain the party’s relationship with traditional institutions and seek the monarch’s royal blessings and counsel ahead of the next general elections. He reaffirmed the group’s recognition of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, as the national leader of the PDP, insisting that its political direction remained firmly anchored on the Rainbow Coalition. item.title: ‘Importing wine doesn’t make you an economist’, Tinubu hits Obi, says Atiku has nothing to offer
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerians to reject opposition presidential candidates, Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, in the 2027 general election, saying they have nothing to offer the country. Tinubu, who spoke through Vice-President Kashim Shettima at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Akure, Ondo State, described the opposition figures as no match for the President. Shettima challenged Obi and Atiku to present their records in public office and policy alternatives to Nigerians, rather than relying on social media campaigns. He said the opposition had failed to demonstrate what it could offer the country. Shettima takes swipe at Atiku, Obi Shettima questioned Atiku’s political standing in his home state of Adamawa, claiming that even former governors of the state were not supporting him. He also criticised Obi, alleging that his campaign relied on what he described as “obnoxious data” rather than verifiable achievements. “The ability to import cheap South African wines does not make one a guru in economics,” he said. The Vice-President described Obi’s tenure as Anambra State governor as mediocre and challenged opposition politicians to identify their major achievements in the past 25 years of democracy. Ondo leaders rally behind Tinubu Shettima said Tinubu enjoyed what he called a “universal elite consensus” in Ondo State, contrasting it with the alleged lack of support for Obi and Atiku in their respective home states. He cited former Ondo State Governor Olusegun Mimiko, former governorship candidate, Chief Olusola Oke, SAN, and member of the House of Representatives, Gboyega Adefarati, as evidence of the APC’s growing political support in the state. He also claimed that former Anambra governors Chris Ngige, Chinwoke Mbadinuju and Willie Obiano, as well as incumbent Governor Charles Soludo, were not aligned with Obi. Shettima projects 1.2 million votes With Ondo’s registered voters put at 2.1 million, Shettima said the APC was targeting at least 1.2 million votes from the 1.8 million residents said to have collected their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described the turnout at the rally as a political statement, recalling similar outings in Cross River, Nasarawa, Akwa Ibom, Rivers, Ebonyi and Jigawa states. Shettima also contrasted the opposition’s activities with what he described as Tinubu’s achievements in the last three and a half years, while commending Ondo APC leaders for putting their differences aside. Aiyedatiwa promises one million votes In his address, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa promised to deliver one million votes for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Aiyedatiwa thanked the President for what he described as progressive policies and interventions, saying Ondo voted massively for Tinubu in 2023 because of his leadership record as governor of Lagos State. item.title: Manchester United ‘Reach Verbal Agreement’ With Ex-Chelsea Coach Pochettino To Replace Carrick
item.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Argentine Mauricio Pochettino to replace embattled Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post, but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Turbulent Reign Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job.
